Enact raises $30M to build force-aware assembly robots

The Zurich startup combines actuators, control and AI for small-batch assembly, with quantitative performance results still undisclosed.

Humanoids Daily ↗23 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

Funding hardware and AI together

Enact Intelligence has emerged with a $30 million pre-seed round co-led by redalpine and Notion Capital. Founded in Zurich in March 2026 by former 1X and Physical Intelligence engineer Manuel Yves Galliker, it is developing actuators, control systems and models together.

Contact feedback for assembly

The intended robot would use forces during movement to judge whether connectors or seals have seated correctly. Learning from demonstrations targets varied, small-batch work that otherwise needs repeated programming. The company briefing says this approach does not require added artificial skin.

Commercial evidence is still missing

Enact says its first motors exist, but has not disclosed accuracy, success rates, cycle times, pricing or delivery dates. Measuring force over 1,000 times per second and reducing training from months to days remain development targets, not demonstrated production performance.
